analysis_steps.goal: Model nebula with LTE radiative transfer

method.value: Axisymmetric disk (inner Keplerian, outer sub-Keplerian + expansion) plus outflow; LTE radiative transfer on ~10^6 cells and 10^4-10^5 rays, convolved with clean beam, compared with maps and PV diagrams

evidence.quote: Typically, we solve the transfer equations following 10$^4$ to 10$^5$ rays, which traverse the cells in which the nebula has been divided.

key_parameters.value: Inclination 70 deg to plane of sky axis, PA -15 deg, X(13CO)=1.5e-5, X(12CO)=1.5e-4

assumptions.value: LTE level populations, constant abundances, axial symmetry, D = 1100 pc

evidence.quote: We assume local-thermal-equilibrium (LTE) populations for the involved rotational levels.

fitting.value: Manual exploration of many configurations; best-fit model chosen by comparison with data and previous results, no formal sampler

evidence.quote: In any case, a high number of different configurations were analyzed.

validation.value: Comparison of predicted channel maps and PV diagrams with data; similarity to Red Rectangle, IW Car

evidence.quote: comparing the predictions with the observational data and other previous results; see predicted maps per velocity channel and position-velocity diagram in Figs. 3 and 5.

evidence.quote: We derived the disk angular momentum by integrating the local momentum of the volume units for the adopted density and velocity laws.

findings_qualitative.value: Equatorial Keplerian disk (inner) with sub-Keplerian expanding outer disk and slow X-shaped outflow

evidence.quote: Our maps of IRAS 08544$-$4431 also show a clearly composite nebula with a disk in rotation and gas in expansion.

claims.hypothesis: IRAS 08544-4431 hosts a rotating disk and slow outflow like other NIR-excess post-AGB stars
claims.experiment: ALMA 12CO/13CO 3-2 maps and LTE nebula modeling
claims.result: Rotation plus expansion reproduced, central mass 1.8 Msun, nebular mass 2e-2 Msun
claims.finding: Composite nebula confirmed, similar to the Red Rectangle

evidence.quote: The main characteristics of our observations and modeling of IRAS 08544$-$4431 are similar to those of better studied objects, confirming our interpretation.

claims.experiment: Compare total mass from rotation with binary orbit parameters
claims.result: 550 pc gives ~1 Msun total and 0.1 Msun primary

evidence.quote: Therefore, this reasoning favors a long distance $\sim$ 1100 pc for IRAS 08544$-$4431

claims.hypothesis: Disk angular momentum came from the binary, shrinking the orbit
claims.experiment: Compare disk J (~13) with binary J (~20)

evidence.quote: we conclude that the distance between the stars has significantly decreased, by a factor  2, owing to the transfer of angular momentum to form the disk.

why_this_method.value: Data and knowledge moderate, so simple models following those of better studied objects

evidence.quote: very detailed models, such as those developed for the Red Rectangle, are not sensible

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Distance 550 pc considered; purely radial velocity field cannot be ruled out

evidence.quote: we cannot rule out a purely radial velocity (as found for IW Car).

limitations_admitted.value: Inner disk and width poorly constrained; mass depends on CO abundance and distance; LTE assumption; temperature uncertain

evidence.quote: Some disk properties are not well determined from the observations, mainly because of the relatively low angular resolution
